purpose: Realistic context pressure for P0-12 (R2): an assistant session mid-way through a working day, with conversation history that includes tool traffic, retrieved document chunks, and live plan state. Profiles select how much of it goes into one request.

assembly.order: instructions (with all catalog tools registered) -> the last N conversation exchanges as transcript entries -> one final prompt containing the first K chunks, then the plan if included, then the probe question
assembly.chunkFormat:
[<doc> - <section>]
<text>, chunks separated by blank lines, under the heading 'Relevant documents:'
assembly.planFormat: 'Current plan: <goal>' followed by one line per step: '<n>. [<status>] <description>' plus ' - <note>' when present
assembly.promptSuffix: Answer using only the conversation and the material above. Do not call any tools. If the answer is not there, say you don't know.
assembly.tokenCounting: Token cost differs by OS (80 vs 107 tokens for the same exchange on macOS 26 vs iOS 27; docs/phase-0-findings.md section 9), so every profile's size is measured per host with SystemLanguageModel.tokenCount, never assumed.
assembly.toolsAreRegisteredButForbidden: The catalog's tools stay registered so they cost their ~1,050 tokens of context (findings section 10), but the probe forbids calling them: with inert tools the model otherwise searches instead of reading the material in its own prompt, which measures tool preference rather than context retention (observed 2026-09-23).

instructions: You are Ledger, the built-in assistant in a work app for a small professional-services company. You help one employee plan their day, find information in their calendar, notes, contacts and company documents, and keep track of multi-step tasks. Use the tools to look things up rather than guessing. Keep answers short and specific, give times in 24-hour format, and quote document wording when the user asks what a policy says. Never invent names, numbers or dates. Actions that create reminders or notes are confirmed by the user before they run.

chunks.text: This policy applies to all employees and contractors who incur costs on the company's behalf. Expenses must be necessary, reasonable, and directly connected to company business. Claims are submitted through the finance portal within 30 days of the expense being incurred, with an itemised receipt for every amount over $25. Claims submitted after 90 days are not reimbursed except with written approval from the Finance Director.

Economy class is the default for all flights. Premium economy may be booked for flights longer than six hours. Business class requires prior approval from a director and is only considered for flights longer than ten hours or where a medical certificate is provided. Rail travel is preferred for journeys under three hours. Ride-share and taxi costs are reimbursed for business travel where public transport is not practical.

Meals are reimbursed up to $75 per day while travelling on company business. This allowance covers breakfast, lunch, dinner and non-alcoholic drinks. Amounts above the daily limit are not reimbursed and cannot be carried over to another day. Alcohol is not reimbursable under the travel meal allowance. Client entertainment is covered separately under section 6.

Employees who work from home at least two days a week may claim up to $450 per financial year for home-office equipment such as chairs, monitors, keyboards and desk lamps. Items remain company property for two years from purchase. Laptops and phones are supplied by IT and cannot be claimed under this allowance. Receipts must show the item, the date and the price paid.

Staff may work remotely up to three days a week by agreement with their manager. Core collaboration hours are 10:00 to 15:00, when everyone should be reachable. Fully remote arrangements are considered case by case and reviewed every six months. Requests are made through the HR portal, and managers respond within ten working days.

Full-time employees receive 20 days of annual leave plus public holidays. Up to 5 unused days may be carried into the next year. Personal leave of 10 days per year covers illness, caring responsibilities and mental health days, and does not require a certificate for absences of up to two consecutive days. Leave is requested in the HR portal at least two weeks ahead where possible.

New starters receive a laptop, a phone and a headset on their first day. Laptop requests for replacements or upgrades are approved by the IT Operations Lead, currently Sam Oyelaran. Lost or stolen devices must be reported to IT within 24 hours so they can be locked remotely. Personal software may not be installed without IT approval.

The Supplier will respond to priority-one incidents within 2 hours and resolve or provide a workaround within 8 hours, 24 hours a day. Priority-two incidents receive a response within one business day. Service availability is measured monthly, with a target of 99.5 percent. If availability falls below target in two consecutive months, the Customer may request a service review.

The agreement runs for an initial term of 12 months from the commencement date and renews automatically for further 12-month periods. Either party may prevent renewal by giving at least 60 days' written notice before the renewal date. Prices may be adjusted at renewal by no more than the published consumer price index plus 2 percent.

Neither party is liable for indirect or consequential loss, including loss of profit or data. Each party's total liability in any 12-month period is capped at the fees paid under the agreement in that period. The cap does not apply to breaches of confidentiality or to liability that cannot be limited by law.

The office is on levels 2 and 3 of 18 Harbour Street. Staff badges open the building from 07:00 to 20:00 on weekdays. Visitors sign in at the ground-floor front desk and are issued a day badge, which must be returned when they leave. Meeting rooms on level 3 are named after birds: Kestrel, Heron and Wren.

The level 2 kitchen has coffee, tea and filtered water. Lockers are available on a first-come basis and must be cleared every Friday. Printing is managed through the Follow-Me queue: send to 'Harbour-Print' and release the job at any printer with your badge. Report building faults to facilities@harbourst.example.

Meeting catering is ordered through Corner Pantry at least 24 hours in advance, with a minimum order of 6 people. Orders can be changed or cancelled free of charge until 16:00 the previous business day. Dietary requirements should be listed per person on the order form. Catering costs are charged to the booking team's cost centre.

Staff connect to the HSStaff network using their company login. The guest network is HSGuest, and the password is tidal-7731. The guest password is rotated quarterly, and the new one is posted on the reception screen. Guest access is limited to web browsing and is isolated from company systems.

Customer data may only be stored in approved systems. It must not be copied to personal devices, personal cloud storage or removable media. Documents classified as Confidential must be shared with named individuals rather than by open link. Suspected data incidents are reported to security@company.example immediately, even if the impact is unclear.

Company accounts require a password of at least 14 characters and multi-factor authentication. Passwords must not be reused across services or shared with colleagues. Password managers approved by IT may be used. Accounts are locked after 10 failed sign-in attempts and unlocked by the IT service desk after identity verification.

profiles.represents: A quick lookup early in a session
A normal mid-session request with retrieval and an active plan
A long working session with generous retrieval
Everything at once: more retrieval than an app should send, to find the ceiling

scoring.availability: A probe's fact is in context when its source is included: exchange >= 12 - profile.exchanges + 1, chunk position <= profile.chunks, plan when profile.plan is true.

outcomes.exceeded: The request threw the context-size error (exceededContextWindowSize on OS 26, contextSizeExceeded on OS 27). This is the P0-12 exhaustion count.
outcomes.recalled: Fact in context, and the answer contains it.
outcomes.missed: Fact in context, but the answer doesn't contain it. Silent degradation: the failure mode that exhaustion counts miss.
outcomes.abstained: Fact not in context, and the answer says it doesn't know. Correct behaviour.
outcomes.hallucinated: Fact not in context, but the answer asserts some other specific value.
outcomes.otherError: Any other thrown error, recorded by type and case.
